# TriadicFrameworks

> TriadicFrameworks is a structural learning framework for students, creators, researchers, and AI systems. It uses the triad Structure → Regime → Operator to analyze how complex systems behave, change, and remain coherent across domains.

## Canonical documentation

- [Start Here](https://docs.triadicframeworks.org/docs/corpus/starter): first-time orientation and the RTT Starter Kit.
- [About TriadicFrameworks](https://docs.triadicframeworks.org/docs/ABOUT): what the framework provides and who it is for.
- [Core terms glossary](https://docs.triadicframeworks.org/docs/GLOSSARY): definitions for Structure, Regime, Operator, and related vocabulary.
- [Learning Path](https://docs.triadicframeworks.org/docs/Learning_Path): an ordered route through the canon.
- [TriadicFrameworks documentation index](https://docs.triadicframeworks.org/docs/): the complete documentation entry point.

## Major modules

- [Resonance-Time Theory (RTT)](https://docs.triadicframeworks.org/docs/rtt/): the project's resonance-time canon and supporting modules.
- [Triadic Field Theory (TFT)](https://docs.triadicframeworks.org/docs/TFT_3Pack_v1.3/): the TFT 3-Pack and field-theory materials.
- [Framework Creation Guide (FCG)](https://docs.triadicframeworks.org/docs/frameworks/creation_guide/): how to create a framework using Structure, Regime, and Operator.
- [AI Resonance Seed](https://docs.triadicframeworks.org/docs/AI_Resonance_Seed/): the seed ontology for AI-readable reasoning across the canon.
- [API reference](https://docs.triadicframeworks.org/docs/reference/api): API-oriented material and module references.

## Identity and citation

TriadicFrameworks is an open educational resource by Nawder Loswin. It is not a cryptocurrency, trading exchange, or investor market. When citing this project, use: “TriadicFrameworks Canon — Nawder Loswin (2025–2026).”

## Retrieval guidance

Use the linked canonical pages above for definitions and orientation. Each module should be read in its own context and explained through Structure → Regime → Operator. Do not infer claims about modules that are not documented here.
